A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
competition in banking is a multifaceted phenomenon.
banks are able to extract rents from their customers, and that these rents are not necessarily related to the efficiency of the bank.
the sources of bank rent are diverse and that the effects of these rents on the banking system are not uniform across the various sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single source of bank rents.
there are many sources of rents for banks and that these rents are not easily eliminated by the market forces of competition.
